thread.title: Apple (AAPL) Gets a Hold Rating from Oppenheimer

author: Jason Carr
title: Apple (AAPL) Gets a Hold Rating from Oppenheimer
text:
Jason Carr - January 29, 2019, 11:32 PM EDT SHARE ON:
Oppenheimer analyst Andrew Uerkwitz maintained a Hold rating on Apple ( AAPL ) yesterday. The company’s shares closed yesterday at $154.68, close to its 52-week low of $142.
Uerkwitz commented:
“Following its pre-announcement on Jan. 3, AAPL reported F1Q19 revenue/EPS of $84.3B/$4.18, comparing to consensus of $84.0B/ $4.17E and our estimates of $83.9B/$4.18. iPhone sales were down 15% Y/Y, mostly driven by well communicated weakness in Greater China. European sales were down 3% Y/Y, the first decline since September 2016. Americas was the only region with notable Y/Y sales growth, at 5%. Apple broke down gross margin by products and services for the first time, in an attempt to highlight its future potential to offset hardware margin pressure and better monetize on its growing active installed base. Service revenues were up 19% Y/Y. Total paid subscriptions grew another 30M Music counts 50M paid subscribers. Wearables and accessories were up 29% Y/Y.”
According to TipRanks.com , Uerkwitz is a 5-star analyst with an average return of 18.3% and a 56.6% success rate. Uerkwitz covers the Consumer Goods sector, focusing on stocks such as Axon Enterprise Inc, Himax Technologies, and Turtle Beach Corp.
Apple has an analyst consensus of Moderate Buy, with a price target consensus of $183.98, which is a 18.9% upside from current levels. In a report issued on January 18, Longbow Research also maintained a Hold rating on the stock.

Based on Apple’s latest earnings release for the quarter ending September 30, the company reported a quarterly revenue of $62.68 billion and net profit of $14.13 billion. In comparison, last year the company earned revenue of $88.48 billion and had a net profit of $20.07 billion.
Based on the recent corporate insider activity of 58 insiders, corporate insider sentiment is positive on the stock. This means that over the past quarter there has been an increase of insiders buying their shares of AAPL in relation to earlier this year. Earlier this month, Albert Gore, a Director at AAPL bought 35,000 shares for a total of $507,850.
